metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#citation: Globally gridded MODIS-TERRA Collection C6.1 Forest and Vegetation Cover Fraction at 0.5 resolution derived at ICDC (https://www.cen.uni-hamburg.de/icdc) based on DiMiceli, C., Sohlberg, R., Townsend, J. (2022) MODIS/Terra Vegetation Continuous Fields Yearly L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061, NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC, https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MOD44B.061, last access: November 1, 2022
metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#comment: Latitude and longitude coordinates per grid cell of the input tiles were computed at UHH based on the work of Benjamin Bechtel, benjamin.bechtel@uni-hamburg.de
metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#institution: Center for Earth System Research and Sustainability (CEN), Integrated Climate Data Center, University of Hamburg
metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#references: [1] https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/products/mod44bv061/; [2] User Guide: https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/documents/1494/MOD44B_User_Guide_V61.pdf; [3] Algorithm Theoretical Basis Document (ATBD): https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/documents/113/MOD44B_ATBD.pdf (Note: This is a very old version from 1999)
metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#standard_name_vocabulary: NetCDF Climate and Forecast (CF) Metadata Convention
metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#summary: From FCF, VCF and non-vegetated land cover fraction data on the MODIS sinusoidal grid at 250 m grid resolution global maps are computed; these contain the grid-cell mean fraction of FCF, VCF or non-vegetated land cover fractions, the variance of these parameter in the grid cell (based on the 250m pixels) and the grid-cell mean retrieval standard deviation are computed. Two additional layers provide the number of valid 250 m pixel values per grid cell. Another three additional layers provide a grid-cell mean quality flag: the smaller the better, and the fractions of the most and second-most encountered quality flag.
metadatos_fuente.NC_GLOBAL#title: MODIS-TERRA Collection 6.1 annual Forest and Vegetation Cover Fraction (FCF and VCF) from LPDAAC: https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/products/mod44bv061/ gridded from sinusoidal grid into an equi-rectangular (Climate Modeling Grid) grid
